title: originshift: US non-preferential rules of origin, compiled from the eCFR
description:
Non-preferential rules of origin, as data. Compiles 19 CFR 102.20 and 102.21 out of the eCFR into a machine-readable corpus, answers which country a good is legally from, and cites the rule it used.

Two corpora, each pinned to a nomenclature vintage. 102.21 governs the origin of every textile and apparel import, from any country, for purposes of the Customs laws (19 CFR 102.21(a)), except as to Israel. 102.20 governs country-of-origin marking for goods of Canada and Mexico under USMCA and NAFTA.

Scope. Per 19 CFR 102.0, Part 102 is confined to marking. For a textile or apparel good, 102.21 governs origin for purposes of the Customs laws and the Chapter 99 provisions key off that determination. For any other good, Section 301 and Section 232 origin turn on the common-law substantial transformation test, which is case law, has no rule table, and is not implemented here. Commerce decides AD/CVD scope. This produces a determination, never a certificate of origin, and does no preferential or FTA qualification.

Provenance. Every record carries the source URL, the eCFR issue date, and the nomenclature vintage it answers under, so a rule can be re-derived after the source is amended and an answer states what it was decided under. Defects found in the source text are reported rather than corrected, with the verbatim text, in the corpus anomalies list.

Validation. Scored against CBP's own HQ rulings, which are binding determinations by the authority whose rules this compiles. Coverage, rule fidelity stratified by era of the ruling, the denominators, the exclusions, and every disagreement in full are published and regenerated by the validator.

Licensing. The code and the compiled corpus are released under Apache-2.0. The underlying sources are United States Government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); the compilation, its structure and its annotations are the author's work.
